_comment: Action-package policy and text for tools/notice_pack.py (`intel.py notice <case>`, the notice_draft tool). The generator reads ONLY stored case artifacts and drafts notices under cases/<case>/notices/; nothing is sent. Every group here is analyst-tunable DATA: the refusal thresholds, the map that decides which cluster binding counts as an owner link, the recipient report pages and the English text per recipient class. The loader fallback is the conservative minimum: confidence `high` required, a contradicted / not_supported premise and a benign_check intake refused, an empty binding map (so every member is excluded rather than accused) and plain fallback text. RULE 1: classes, public provider pages and placeholder text only, never case data.

policy._comment: Refusal thresholds. min_confidence: the lowest assessment confidence (low < moderate < high) a notice may be drafted on. A value that is not in confidence_order refuses every draft. Lowering it lets a weaker judgment name a party in a notice sent outside the team; raise, never lower, without the case owner's agreement.

refuse_attribution_levels._comment: assessment.json attribution_level values that never produce a notice. same-kit says the sites share a toolkit, not an owner, and inconclusive says nothing was established; a notice on either would name a party the evidence does not support.

refuse_premise_verdicts._comment: assessment.json premise_verdict values (harness/schemas.py: supported, partially_supported, not_supported, contradicted, inconclusive) that refuse the whole draft. A run whose own collection contradicts, or does not support, the claim it was given must not turn that claim into a notice.

refuse_target_classes._comment: scope.json target_class values (WebPivot/references/intake.json target_classes: confirmed_scam, suspected_scam, threat_actor_infra, victim_host, benign_check, unknown) that refuse the whole draft. benign_check is a legitimacy question about a business, not an accusation; an abuse notice out of it is exactly the unfounded fraud verdict that class warns against.

confidence_order._comment: Assessment confidence scale, weakest first (harness/schemas.py Assessment.confidence). A value missing from this list is treated as below every threshold, so the generator refuses.

binding_rel_classes._comment: clusters.json binding indicator RELATION -> rungs.json identifier class (then selector_types.rung_for decides owner/kit/neighbour). Graded PER HOST on the relations that host itself holds to the indicator (binding `rels_by_domain`, else the host's own edges in the knowledge base) — never on the union `rels`, which merges every domain sharing it; a host whose own relation cannot be established is excluded. A key `rel|type` is tried first (type = the part of the indicator before the first colon: email, phone, org, person, indicator), then the bare `rel`, then binding_prefix_classes. A binding that maps to no class is kit (rung_for default), so an unmapped relation can only EXCLUDE a member, never admit one. A member is a notice subject only when an owner-graded binding it holds is also held, owner-graded, by another member, linking it to the seed inside the seed's cluster.

binding_prefix_classes._comment: Indicator PREFIX (the label inside an `indicator:<prefix>:<value>` binding) -> rungs.json identifier class, used when the relation itself is not mapped above. Tracker labels are the ingest_webpivot relation keys (selector_types._TRACKER_RUNG); ads ids stay kit.

platform_report_pages._comment: Social network / app store -> the platform's public help or reporting page, printed on each platform checklist. Keys are the social_platforms.json names wp_extract writes under artifacts.socials, plus google_play / app_store for artifacts.app_downloads. A platform with no entry prints `the platform's own reporting page`; add it here when you meet it.

cdn_abuse_contacts._comment: Edge / CDN provider name as dns.ip_classification[].provider spells it (lower-cased) -> the provider's public abuse-report page. A provider with no entry gets a notice with no contact and says so; the analyst finds the page by hand.

templates._comment: English text per recipient class: {title, body}. Placeholders are filled by notice_pack.py; an unknown placeholder is left verbatim. {case} case id, {recipient} recipient name, {subjects} bulleted subject list, {evidence} bulleted evidence list (capture time + SHA-256), {attribution_level} / {confidence} from assessment.json, {bluf} the assessment's bottom line — REFERRAL PACK ONLY: analyst prose is not written for a registrar, host, CDN, bank or platform, and notice_pack fills it for no other class. {report_page} platform page, {checklist} platform items, {accounts} payment accounts, {timeline} dated events, {ioc_bundle} IOC files, {excluded} a one-line COUNT of hosts deliberately left out (their names live only in notices/index.json, and every excluded host and its subdomains is replaced in every notice). Keep the compromise text free of any takedown request: its recipient is a victim.

registrar.title: Abuse report: domain registration(s) at {recipient}

host.title: Abuse report: content served from your network ({recipient})

cdn.title: Notice: site(s) behind your edge service ({recipient})

platform.title: Platform report checklist: {recipient}

bank.title: Fraud report: payment account(s) at {recipient}

referral.title: Referral pack: {case}

compromise.title: Security notice: your site appears to serve content you did not publish
